topicName: Connect: Connecting to external Kubernetes clusters
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Connect: Connecting to External Kubernetes Clusters in Google Cloud (GCP)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial outlines how to connect external Kubernetes clusters to Google Cloud (GCP) using Connect. Connect enables you to manage and observe your Kubernetes clusters, regardless of where they are running, from a central point within the Google Cloud Console."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A running Kubernetes cluster outside of Google Cloud (e.g., on-premises, AWS, Azure)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Google Cloud project with the necessary permissions (e.g., `roles/container.registerer`, `roles/gkehub.admin`)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The `gcloud` CLI installed and configured to point to your Google Cloud project."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Sufficient network connectivity between your external Kubernetes cluster and Google Cloud."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enable the GKE Hub API"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The GKE Hub API is required to register your external cluster with Google Cloud. You can enable it using the `gcloud` CLI:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"gcloud services enable gkehub.googleapis.com"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Register Your External Cluster"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Register your external cluster using the `gcloud` CLI. Replace `<cluster-name>` with a name for your cluster within Google Cloud, and `<kubeconfig-path>` with the path to your cluster's kubeconfig file."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"gcloud container fleet memberships register <cluster-name> \\\n    --kubeconfig=<kubeconfig-path> \\\n    --context=<kubeconfig-context>"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Note: The `--context` flag specifies the context within the kubeconfig file to use for connecting to the cluster. If omitted, the current context is used."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Deploy the Connect Agent"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"After registering the cluster, you need to deploy the Connect Agent to your external cluster. The registration process will output a command to deploy the agent. It will look similar to this:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"kubectl apply -f <manifest-url>"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Execute this command on your external Kubernetes cluster. This will deploy the necessary resources for the Connect Agent to communicate with Google Cloud."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Verify the Connection"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"After deploying the Connect Agent, verify that the connection is established. You can do this by checking the status of the membership in the Google Cloud Console or using the `gcloud` CLI:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"gcloud container fleet memberships describe <cluster-name>"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Look for a `state` field in the output. If the connection is successful, the state should be `ACTIVE`."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Accessing Your Cluster in the Google Cloud Console"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the cluster is registered and the Connect Agent is running, you can access your external Kubernetes cluster from the Google Cloud Console. Navigate to the Kubernetes Engine -> Clusters page. Your registered cluster should be listed there, allowing you to view its resources and manage it from the console."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Troubleshooting"},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"If the cluster does not appear in the Google Cloud Console, double-check the network connectivity between your external cluster and Google Cloud."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verify that the Connect Agent is running correctly in your external cluster. Check the logs of the agent pods for any errors."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure that the service account used by the Connect Agent has the necessary permissions to access Google Cloud resources."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"By following these steps, you can successfully connect your external Kubernetes clusters to Google Cloud using Connect. This allows you to manage and observe all your Kubernetes clusters from a single pane of glass, simplifying your multi-cloud or hybrid cloud management strategy."}]
